target_text: Ululu plialiaini upa lerni-tgara lerni de patke'a ida nora muanke'a ida rmehlima; muanke'a nwawa Rettiau, patke'a nwawa Rarlay.
source_text: A long time ago, in the time of our ancestors, a man and a woman were married. The man's name was Rettiau and the woman's name was Rarlay.

target_text: Hare de maran Wetgai Ilia re.
source_text: They were of the nobility clan called Wetgai Ili.

target_text: Noka rrora a'nani muanke'a woru; yanulu nwawa Rettiau Lay ma gari nwawa Rettiau Ru'ru, yoma rrora amni Rettiau pede riwra Rettiau Ru'ru Rettiau Lay, mere plollolli de yanulu nwawa Lay me gari nwawa Ru'ru.
source_text: In time they had two sons, the elder was named Rettiau Lay and the younger named Rettiau Ruru. They were called this after their father because his name was Rettiau. However, the elder was really named Lay and the younger was named Ruru.

target_text: Noma rtera-rlahga pa rla'awa tuwgeni-lawangen wia pa nhi'noka ror amni rwed yatru ida.
source_text: The years went by and they grew up under their parents care. One day when they were older they made a fish trap with their father.

target_text: Lla'pa lera ida na Rarlay e namehra.
source_text: Then one day their mother Rarlay became sick.

target_text: Namehra pa nahmena na'ana-nemnu.
source_text: She was so sick she did not want to eat.

target_text: Nakotla hawni niwra: "Au'una iwu ati nampa kalwieda pa mhuopantek it a'nani rrora rla rtollia yatru."
source_text: So she said to her husband, "I need to eat some shark's liver and then I'll feel better. Go tell our children to set the fish trap."

target_text: Noka a'nani rrora rla rtol yatru, pa rla de de yatru enni iwu ida.
source_text: So the two children went and set the trap and caught a shark.

target_text: Noka rrora rwahi'pa rodia iwu pa rmaiwia,
source_text: They went to get it and bring it home,

target_text: Mere rror edon rod wehla.
source_text: but they had forgotten to bring a machete.

target_text: Noka yanulu natiakrer iwu na gari nma nal wehla.
source_text: The eldest stayed at the trap and guarded the fish while the youngest went to fetch the machete.

target_text: Gari nma nala wehla de iwu nhari lirni pa nakotla yanulu: "Ei mtulan pa msiaini a'u de muolindoinia a'u la."
source_text: After he left, the shark opened its mouth and said to the elder brother, "Have pity on me and help me and let me go."

target_text: Ailia'awa a noh'u-a rai'yu.
source_text: I will go to my home.

target_text: Pena lera ida mela id pa, ler lola mel lol pa mhuopla-mliar pa mlier la komlorni-pah'a metni demade de mpuolu-mpuak a'u pena ahgima rie o'a, aitulan ti o'a, hgimpai-muanatg o'a."
source_text: If some day when you are sailing you run into trouble then call on me to come help you and I will.'

target_text: Noka yanulu na nolindoini iwu la.
source_text: So the elder brother let the shark go.

target_text: Garni nod wehla pa nmai de de iwu nmolu olekwa.
source_text: A little while later the younger brother arrived with the machete, but the shark was already gone.

target_text: Noka garni natiana niwra: “Kaka iwu etla meni?”
source_text: So the younger brother asked, “Older brother, where is the shark?"

target_text: Nakot niwra: “Iwu agolindoini oleka la."
source_text: "I let the shark go," he answered.

target_text: Noka rrora rla'awa.
source_text: Then they went home.

target_text: Rla'awa noka inni-amni ratiana riwra: “Enmi erla meni?"
source_text: Then they went home. When they got home their parents asked them, “Where is the fish you caught?"

target_text: "Amakleh eni, yatru nakleh eni.”
source_text: "We did not catch anything."

target_text: Dewade inni nawenanwa niwra: “Kekeʼenkua ra rwaklili-rwakdiori, rputra-rpalka."
source_text: Then the mother was angry and said, “You kids are lying."

target_text: Agatga de yatru na’eni iwu na’nama mmiai miala wehla pa mial la mpiarowta-mpi’anna.
source_text: I know you caught a shark and then came home to get a machete to cut it up.

target_text: Ne miy miolindoinia iwu olek la pa mimpiutra-mpialka a'u pa o dodo’on di de musti rwenan miy.”
source_text: You let the shark go and then you lied to me. Now you must be killed.”

target_text: Noka nakotla hawni pa rwenna kekeʼenku’a rrora.
source_text: Then she told her husband to kill the two children.

target_text: “Yana ramori-radaria yoma rwaklili-rwakdiori, rputra-rpalk olek it wa."
source_text: Do not let them live because they have lied and deceived us."

target_text: Noka amni nsainia a'nani rrora.
source_text: The father felt sorry for his two children,

target_text: Mere llernohora hawni.
source_text: but he obeyed his wife.

target_text: Mere amni nsainia rpa nhi'a gerni wareherni, nhi' gotgot la rrora.
source_text: However, he felt pity on them, so he packed them some food for the trip.

target_text: Nawew la rrora pa: “Kekwali die mro' miwlarwia.”
source_text: Then he said to them, “In a little while you two run away."

target_text: Lera nmellaw noka amni npona wehlani pa naploklokar na’nama lla nhi’a ud liola woru ma nkeni gera la rpu'pu woru pa nkenia la dudgenni wawannu pa nhiʼtarga.
source_text: When it became dark he filed his machete to make it real sharp. Then he got two banana trunks and two coconut shells and put them in the boys' beds.

target_text: A'nani rrora ranina pa mela letgara dewade de namatdoinia a’nani rrora pa rrora rawlarwia, nhakar gotgota pa rima-rima naʼala gotgotni pa rawlarwia na’nama, na'ala wehla pa rrahyetia ud liola id wa demade de nhurdoinia ger rpuʼpu id la.
source_text: In the middle of the night he woke the two boys up so they could escape. He gave them each some food and told them to run off. Then the father took his machete and began to hack at one of the banana trunks and pour out the liquid from the coconut shell.

target_text: Demade hawni niwra: “Hniakarmi hade, mmiati-mmiati, keke'en maka edon kaʼunna-kamtaʼata inni nor amni."
source_text: While he was doing this his wife heard the noise and said, “That's what you get children -- death - when you do not obey and respect your parents."

target_text: Demade de muankeʼeni na' owan la wehla pa ndawreti owaʼan udi lola id wa demade de nhurdioini gera lari id la wa.
source_text: Then the father took up the machete again to hack the other banana trunk and pour out the milk from the second coconut shell.

target_text: Demade de hawni niwra: “Hniakarmi hade, miati-miati."
source_text: Then the wife again, "That's what you get, death."

target_text: Noka keke'enku'a rrora rlergot pa rawlarwia ne muanke'a ntot pa na'ala gera pa nkuhi-nho'ordoinia lewu wawannu totpa riwra e nkuhi-nho'ora rara.
source_text: When he finished the father got some water to wash off the bed so people would think that he was washing away the blood.

target_text: Keke'enku'a rawlarwia, rrora rla'awa, rodi gerni-wareherni pa rrora rala'awa, rala'awa, rala'la mel di pa nodi pa repar pa lera npahna pa rrora raplarwa.
source_text: In the meantime, the two boys ran and ran carrying their food. They kept going through the night until the heat of the next day when they got very hungry.

target_text: Raplarwa noka yanulu nhi'a gotgotni pa rrora ra'ana de gotgotawu.
source_text: The elder opened his food up to eat, but it was ashes.

target_text: Noka gari niwra: "Kaka demade tsi'teka a gotgo'tu."
source_text: Then the younger said, "Brother, let us try mine."

target_text: Rhi' gotgotni de gari gotgotni de wetra'a, noka rrora ra'ana.
source_text: When they opened it, it was corn. Then they ate it.

target_text: Ra'an pa nhoru noka rrora rala'awa.
source_text: When they were done eating they continued on.

target_text: Rala'aw-rala'aw-rala'aw-rala'a nek pa nhi'iwa de rlernana ma'nu ida riwra ma'nu warta.
source_text: They continued on and on until they came upon a bird called the 'Bird of the West' (which gives power).

target_text: Noka yanulu nwa'ala, nwa'ala-nwa'alneka mere ta'eni nwa'alnana nwa'ala sala-sala.
source_text: Once they saw it, the elder brother tried to hit it with a rock. He tried and tried, but he could not hit it.

target_text: Ma'nu mana edona nnem wali.
source_text: Even though the bird did not even fly away.

target_text: Noka gari niwra: "Kaka demada wua'alteka!"
source_text: Then the younger brother said, "Let me have a try."

target_text: Gari nteman watu dewade de nwa'alnana pa ma'nu ntuinierun noka na'ala pa nkopildoini matni olli pa llumga.
source_text: So he picked up a rock and threw it at the bird. He hit it straight away and the bird fell. Then he ran over and he plucked out the eye ball (where the power was) and swallowed it.

target_text: Rala' owa'an rala' owa'an rala' owa'an rala owa'ana lla' pa rler la talla hniakarni.
source_text: Then they continued on and on until they came to a branch in the road.

target_text: Talla ida nnehna malwiru, ida nnehna malgana.
source_text: One branch went to the left and the other to the right.

target_text: Noka yanulu lola talan malwiru, llala' noka lernana maka khur miaha-ktor leli.
source_text: The eldest decided that he would take the road that branched to the left. After going down the left road he soon came upon a man who was a goldsmith.

target_text: Noka yanulu lla' pa nahaka kniari la noka rreinana ra'nana pa rre'ela nhuri maha-ntor leli, na gari nanpena llola malgana nalola-nala' nek pa lla'awa nu'nu ida hananni.
source_text: So the eldest asked the goldsmith for work. The man agreed and gave the elder brother a job, helping him make things out of gold. The younger brother decided to take the road that went to the right and he continued on until he came to a banyan tree (a place of authority and knowledge),

target_text: Lla'awa nu'nu hananni, ne gera ida etla nu'nu nainni.
source_text: Under the tree was a well.

target_text: Noka happe'a Mnietu nmai pa ntip gera, ntip ger noka keke'en di na'ala nu'nu wo'a pa nwa'ala la kewtu ralamni.
source_text: It was not long before an old woman from the nobility clan of Mnietu came to draw water. The younger (brother) took a banyan fruit and threw it into her dipper.

target_text: Noka happe'a niwra: "Ei onu-ma'nu ri rhi'a kdedeh neka ger di wa."
source_text: The old woman said, "The birds are making this water dirty."

target_text: Noka na'ala pa ntowurdoinia la.
source_text: Then she poured the water out.

target_text: Noka ntipu owa'ana, ntipu owa'an dewade keke'en di na'ala nu'nu wo'a pa naklu owa'ana la kewtu ralamni.
source_text: Then she drew water again, and then again the youth took a banyan fruit and threw it into her dipper again.

target_text: Noka happe'a niwra: "Onu-ma'nu ri a rhi'a kdedeh neka ger di wa.
source_text: Then the old woman said: "This bird keep making this water dirty.""

target_text: Noka ntowurdoini owa'ana la."
source_text: Then she poured out the water again

target_text: Emkade pa re'eni wotelu dewade happe'a namkek la heyanna.
source_text: This happened three times and then the old woman looked up into the tree.

target_text: Namkeknana keke'en di noka niwra: "Up ei, omdiella meni, muernu ukleha upa-a'ana pa tot la lla'pa tsoliwutu, atiera-liah'u."
source_text: She saw the boy and said, "Grandchild, where did you come from? Come down and stay with me for I do not have any children."

target_text: Noka keke'en di nerun pa nora rla'awa.
source_text: So he came down from the tree and went with her.

target_text: La la'noka nwahaurnohora emkade-emkadi la inni-amni.
source_text: As they walked they talked and talked. He told her about his parents,

target_text: Noka upni niwra: "Itro'a tsoliwut lia hadi wa pa ukleh up-a'na wal pia tro'a tsoliwutu."
source_text: and she said he ought to come live with her since she had no children.

target_text: Noka rora rden nek la hande wa pa nhi' pa llawan wa, mere namno'a-namrara.
source_text: So they stayed together and the younger brother grew up. However, he contracted a disease.

target_text: Noka ler ida na ratlin de kakni di e lernana makhuri miaha-ktor leli, rre'ela nhuri miaha-ntor leli.
source_text: Then one day he heard that his brother was with a goldsmith and was learning to make gold jewelry.

target_text: Noka garni nakotla upni: "Upa a'u la umkekteka makhuri miaha-ktor leli ri na."
source_text: So he said to the old woman, "Grandma, I want to go see this goldsmith."

target_text: Noka upni niwra: "Yowa de mlia'teka!"
source_text: The grandmother said: "Go have a look."

target_text: Noka lla'awa dewade garni nayapi a'altawi la ma'nu maka ira rwa'alnana totpena nala la kakni, pa kakni namkeka totpena kakni natiana niwra: "He' makala a'altawi ma'nu warat dina?" totpena natga garni.
source_text: Then he went and wove some palm leaves together and made it into the shape of the bird which he had hit with the stone. He wanted to give it to his elder brother as a sign so that he would look at it and say, "Who is it that gives me these palm leaves woven like the 'Bird of the West'?" He wanted his brother to recognize that it was him.

target_text: Mere kakni namkeka a'altawi ma'nu warta, noka na'ala pa nhi'a la maha na edon natian wali garni wali.
source_text: However, when the elder brother saw the image of the bird he just looked at it and took it and made it into gold, but did not even ask about his younger brother.

target_text: Noka garni nmaiwa pa nakotla upni niwra: "Upa ahgi'a ka'ku totpa natg a'u mere rre'a-ntarwa pa naplinu a'au wa.
source_text: Then the younger brother came home and said to the old woman, "I tried to make it so my older brother would recognize me but he is already rich and does not (want to) recognize me any more.

target_text: Na' to'o la a'altawi mak a'uyapia la ma'nu wa rla pa nkenia la mahani."
source_text: He just took the leaves I wove like the bird and made it into gold."

target_text: Noka upni niwra: "Takot pa nre'a-ntarg olekwa pa naplinu o'o wa."
source_text: The old woman said: "He has already become so wealthy that he has forgotten you."

target_text: Rrora rholiwutu-rletwutu nek la hande pa lera ida na ne kota-de'eta nwattiawua Melai-Watkali, nmai de de riwra rai Melai Watkali nhi'a weta-weta, pa ha meni lla'pa nwetnana demade nora a'nani patke'a ida rmehlima, yoma a'nani patke'a wonem era re.
source_text: So the younger brother continued to stay with the old woman until one day news came from Melai-Watkali that the king of Melai-Watkali had made a riddle. Whoever was able to solve the riddle could marry one of his six daughters.

target_text: Noka kakni Rettiau Lay di nwetrul lie'u-ndadli lliara pa totpena nla lla' pa nareri-nawaka maran Melai a'nani id pa nora rmehlima, hornama nwetnana kokkoi hade me weta-weta.
source_text: The elder brother, Rettiau Lay planned to sail there and try to solve the riddle so that he could marry one of the king's daughters.

target_text: Pa puou mniotni riy ida woru ror wali.
source_text: There were other people on the boat also.

target_text: Noma garni Rettiau Ru'ru di natlinnana noka nakotla upni: "Upa a'u la wuatena au pa agora mla' Melai."
source_text: The younger brother found out about this and said to the old woman, "Grandma, I would like to go along to Melai-Watkali."

target_text: Mere upni nakotiwra: "Up ei, yana mlia'a ma makre'a-maktarga hare pa rla rwahaka mehlimni-marya'ani na omlia' wali."
source_text: But the old woman said: "Grandchild, do not go off with those rich people to get married,"

target_text: Mere upni nahmen memna nakot niwra: "Upa a'u la'a, a'u edona lia uhaka mehli'mu-marya'u mere a'u lia umkek to'a."
source_text: But he really wanted to go. He said: "I do not want to go get married. I just want to go have a look,"

target_text: Noka upni niwra: "Dema mlia mpuate'nu pa mlia'awa."
source_text: Then the old woman said: "Then go with them."

target_text: Noka lla nwatena pa rreinana niwra: "A'u lia edon uhaka a mehli'mu ma a'u lia umkek to'a noha-rai."
source_text: Then he went asked for a ride saying: "I'm not trying to get married, I just want to go have a look at that land."

target_text: Noka rreinana-rra'nana pa la la' pa nora rhopal mere ndella hota rria'geni nattiaka rria'a rrietni yoma namno'a-namrara.
source_text: Then they allowed him to sail with them but he just stayed in the hull of the boat because of his disease.

target_text: Noka rla'awa.
source_text: Then they left.

target_text: Rla'awa Melai wa pa kakni rerun la keranni wa.
source_text: When they got to Melai-Watkali, the elder brother got off and went ashore.

target_text: Rerun la keranni pa rhoi-rtania pa nhoruwa noka rakotiwra: "Yowa, makota de de u'upu-a'anu pa miora mmiehlima hornama mikwietnana weta-wet hadi ma kokkoia di."
source_text: After they served him food, the king said, "Yes, you can marry one of my daughters if you guess the riddle."

target_text: Noka maran Melai nhi'a petu wu'unu wonema pa nhi'a pa namdiddidni pa riy raplinga onni meni, ltutnu meni.
source_text: Then the king took six pieces of bamboo and made them smooth so no one knew which piece was from the middle or which piece was from the end of the bamboo.

target_text: Pa nhopan pa rakwieta.
source_text: Then the king told him to guess.

target_text: Rakwieta mere raplinga.
source_text: The elder brother tried to guess, but did not know (the answer).

target_text: Noka maran Melai nhopan pa rala wawi a'nani wonema pa nmai na'nama nhopan pa niwra: "Mikwietteka wawi a'nani yanulu ed ha meni ma, letgara ha meni ma, gari ha meni."
source_text: Then the king of Melai-Watkali brought out six pigs, saying, "Guess which one is the oldest, middle and youngest."

target_text: Noma rakwieta mere edona rakwietnana, raplinga.
source_text: So the elder brother tried to guess again, but he did not know so he guessed wrong.

target_text: Noka rai nakota niwra: "Riy rhoruwa?"
source_text: Then the king said, "Is there no one else (from the boat to guess the riddle)?"

target_text: "Ei riy hadamonna, riy hadamonan la puou."
source_text: "That is all, there is no one else in the boat," (the elder brother replied)

target_text: Ne rai niwra: "Yan riy erla de mpiolga pa nmai."
source_text: The king said, "There must be someone; call him to come,"

target_text: Nakot niwra: "Ei riy id etla mere namno'a-namrara."
source_text: He answered, "There is one person, but he is diseased,"

target_text: Noka rai niwra: "Namno'a-namrar mana riy mormioria pa mlia mpiolga pa yana nakwietnana kokkoi rina."
source_text: The king said, "It does not matter if he is diseased, he is still a person. Go call him, he might be able to solve the riddle."

target_text: Noka rhopan pa rla rpolga.
source_text: Then they told them to go call him.

target_text: Muanke'a ida lla npolga nakot niwra: "Ei muerun la!"
source_text: The man who went to call him said, "Come on down!"

target_text: Noka nerun la wa, noma niwra: "A'u la ulg o'a ma plet pa mtiy."
source_text: When the younger brother came off the boat (the man) said, "I'm going on ahead, you follow quickly."

target_text: Noka nayalindoinia pol yatni-rain yatni pa nerun la keranni pa lla'awa.
source_text: Then the younger brother changed his dirty clothes and got off the boat to go (follow the man).

target_text: Lla lla'pa nden ma'ta la ppuohra gaini, edona lla' ma'ata leta ralamni de nwatromnana patke' ida (happe' ida).
source_text: While he was still at the gate, before he even had a chance to go into the village, he met an old woman.

target_text: Happe' di nwawa Puilioi-Romloi.
source_text: This woman's name was Puilioi-Romloi.

target_text: Noka happe' di nakotla niwra: "Upa omlia meni?"
source_text: She said to him, "Grandchild, where are you going?"

target_text: "Up ei, rai npolg a'u pa ailia lla' pa rakot hya-hya'a, a'u ge lia'teka."
source_text: "Grandma, the king came and called me to come. He wants to say something to me, I had better go see."

target_text: Noka happe' di nakotla niwra: "Upa omlia de omukwieta kokkoi petu rahlanu wonema ma wawi a'nani wonema.
source_text: Then the old woman said to him, "When you go to guess the six pieces of bamboo and the six piglets.

target_text: Omlia mukwieta, omlia la' de mumkek nek pa llaran mota ntai la petu honi id de de petu onni hade pa emkade mammain nek pa lla genia petu honi.
source_text: When you are guessing make sure you look and see where the blue fly lands. The piece of bamboo it lands on will be the end. Then it will land on the middle and then on the other end.

target_text: Wawi a'na mana emkade wali.
source_text: The same with the pigs.

target_text: Mumkek nek pa llaran mota ntai la wawi meni de wawi a'nani yanulu hade, ntai owa'an la han meni de mak lernohora yanulu, letgara, mak lernohora letgara, gari, mumkek nek pa llaran mota ntai la ha meni de mukwiet hade, mliernohora."
source_text: It will land on the eldest first, then the middle one and then on the youngest. Make sure you look where the blue fly lands and then guess it."

target_text: "Yowa."
source_text: (He answered), "Okay"

target_text: Noka lla'wa.
source_text: Then he went.

target_text: Lla'awa pa la' noka rhopan namtatna nhornioka rai nakot niwra: "Hare honnona rakwieta kokkoi mere ta'eni rwetnana pede tre' ma'ta omuemmeh'a pa dodo'on di pa ompwetnana de omuora a'nu ida mmiehlima."
source_text: When he got there he was asked to be seated and then the king said, "Everyone has tried to guess the riddle, but they have not been able do it. You are the only one left. Have a try so you can marry one of my daughters."

target_text: Noka rla rala petu wu'u matnemnemni pa nmai noka namkek nek pa llaran mota ntai la ha meni dewade nakotiwra: "Petu onni hadi, rahlanu letgarni hadi na tutnu hadi."
source_text: Then they brought out the six pieces of bamboo. The younger brother looked to see where the blue fly landed and then said, "This is the end piece, this is the middle and this is the other end."

target_text: Noka rpolu owa'ana wawi a'na rwonema rmai pa nakwieta de namkek nek pa llaran mota ntai la wawi a'nani noka niwra: "Wawi a'nani yanulu eda di."
source_text: Then they called again for the six piglets to come so he could guess. Then he looked where the blue fly landed. Then he said, "This is the eldest."

target_text: Llaran mota ntai owa'an la ida: "A, mak lernohora yanulu ed hadi."
source_text: Then the blue fly landed on another. (So he said,) "This one is the second eldest."

target_text: Llaran mota ntai owan la ida: "A, letgara hadi."
source_text: Then the blue fly landed on another. (So he said) "This is the middle one."

target_text: Emkade pa lla'awa gari pa gari hoho'a dewade nwetnana oleka kokkoi wa.
source_text: In that manner he continued and solved the whole riddle by guessing which one was younger until he got to the very youngest.

target_text: Noka rai niwra: "Mpwetnan oleka kokkoi pa a'nu wonem hare pa rmai pa mpualiria!
source_text: Then the king said, "You have solved the riddle. I have six daughters. Come and choose!"

target_text: A o sukmu la ha meni.
source_text: Which one do you like?

target_text: Mere mukwiet ulga, a' a'nu wonema re yanulu ha meni, letgara ha meni, gari ha meni, pa ompwetnana nanpena muor ida mmiehlima."
source_text: But first you must guess which one is the oldest, the middle and the youngest."

target_text: Noka ne'era a'nani re, mere edona re'era naplollola, gari ndella handi na, yanulu ndella handi na, letgara ndella handi.
source_text: Then the king lined up his daughters, but not according to age. He mixed them up.

target_text: Noka nakwieta, namkek nek pa llaran mota ntai la riy id dohoni dewade de niwra: "A yanulu eda hadi."
source_text: Then the younger brother attempted this final riddle. He looked at where the blue fly landed on one of the girl's hair and said, "This is the oldest."

target_text: Pa llaran mota nnem pa ntai owa'an la id dohoni de niwra: "Maklernohora yanulu hadi."
source_text: Then the blue fly landed on another one's hair. Then he said, "This is the next to the oldest,"

target_text: Pa llaran mota nnem pa ntai owa'an la id dohoni dewade niwra: "A letgara hadi la."
source_text: The blue fly landed on another one's hair so he said, "This is the middle (child)."

target_text: Emkade mammain pa nakwietnan mommuoga dewade rai niwra: "O mukwietnana oleka kokkoi ri wa pa o ralammu niwra muora a' a'nu meni de."
source_text: He continued on like this until he solved the whole riddle. Then the king said, "You have solved the riddle. You may choose which ever daughter you would like."

target_text: Noka nakotiwra: "Gari."
source_text: He said, "The youngest,"

target_text: Noka nor gari rmehlim pa.
source_text: Then the two of them got married.

target_text: Nor gari rmehlim pa rwahi'a-rwayodi pa rwaho'o-rwatierun pa rawallia Lgon wa.
source_text: Then the two of them got married then they prepared to return to Luang.

target_text: Mere rai a'na di edon nemun gera na nemun mammaini norkohola.
source_text: But the king's daughter would not drink water, only the milk from young coconuts.

target_text: Noka rken norkohol la puou.
source_text: So they loaded the boat with young coconuts,

target_text: Me rhi'a tniernu totpena rai a'nani patke'a ndella puou wawannu.
source_text: And they made a tent so the king's daughter would stay on the boat's deck.

target_text: Ne kakni Rettiau Lay di nwaror oleka klili-kdiori ohpa-lahara totpena na'ala patke'eni yoma ralamni namehra la garni.
source_text: But the elder brother Rettiau Lay (felt angry and hurt), so he schemed of a way to deceive his younger brother and to take his new wife.

target_text: Noka rha'atla puou pa rhopalwa.
source_text: Then they got on board the boat to sail.

target_text: Rhopal noka ankoda hadi ma kakni di nawew la puou mniotni: "La' de de miy de mommuou wehla ta'wa re honnona, mkien nieka prahni la tio'ora.
source_text: When they (were about) to sail, the elder brother and the captain said to those on the boat, "When we go, hide all of your machetes and knives, leave only the ax out.

target_text: Mere prahni de mhi'a pa nkalkiali, totpena italla tsapil nora de de omriana de natliehudoin la."
source_text: But make the handle a bit loose so that when he takes it to open the coconut (for his wife) the blade will come off."

target_text: Noka puou mniotni rade' mommuou wehla ta'wa re honnona, prahni nmemmeh'a ndella tio'ora.
source_text: Then the crew hid all the knives and machetes and left only the ax out.

target_text: Noka rhopalwa.
source_text: Then they set sail.

target_text: Rhopal pa rmaiwa hletan letgar wa dewade de patke'a ttiernu keran pa nhopna rhi' nor pa nemnu, nhopan muanke'eni di natian wehla ta'wa pa ralla rhapil nora, riwra: "A wehla hadamonna, ta'wa hadamonna, e prahni id etla pa mualla mhuapil nora."
source_text: When they had left the shore behind and were over the deep blue water, the girl got thirsty and ordered them to get a coconut ready for her to drink. She told her husband to get a knife or machete to cut open the coconut, but the crew said there were none. There was only an ax available to cut open the coconut.

target_text: Noka na'ala prahni di pa niwra nhapil la puou ralamni, kakni ankoda niwra: "Ei yana mhi'a kdeha puou di, mhuaplia la puou aratni."
source_text: Then his brother, the boat driver, said, "Hey, do not get this boat dirty. Cut it open on the edge of the boat."

target_text: Noka nhap lia la puou aratni pa nhap lia pa rran la prahni emkadewa de prahni natliehudoin la pa ntunierun la hletna wikni.
source_text: Then the younger brother took the ax to cut open the coconut on the boat's edge, but the blade fell off and sunk deep down into the sea.

target_text: Dewade kakni nakotla: "Mlia mual memna a prahni'u, ma a'a ge donna uhaka kupna-kai leli-mah dom la prahni hnierannu, mlia mual memna a prahni'u la hletna wikni."
source_text: Then the elder brother said, "You go get my ax head. I do not want money or gold things in exchange for it so go to the bottom of the sea and get my ax head."

target_text: Dewade garni nherieriwia pa nmela pa nakotla hawni: "Kekwali de ailia gala prahni mere na'ala patke'a kdielli pa nakdielia. Then he took the girl's ring off and put it on his finger."
source_text: Then the younger brother was quiet until night time. Then he said to his wife, "In a little while I will go get the ax head." Then he took the girl's ring off and put it on his finger.

target_text: Lla'pa Orgahi-Ora'a nayoryori a'u de a'u wali, mere ailia pa muati-muoli hgo'a tiawu de de takot pa."
source_text: If God wills to protect me I will return, but I cannot control whether I will return or am lost in the sea."

target_text: Ne muor neka puou mniotni mlia'awa lla' pa amuormiori de mpieiwei-mniarnar a'u pa nodia pa a'u wali mere edonan de takot pa!
source_text: You go on with the rest of those on the boat. Wait for me to return, in case I live to return. However if I die and am lost at sea that is beyond my control.

target_text: Emkadewa pa lla'awa puou li'irnu pa repreparreria pa nmer la tipur dewade npollia Uplerlawna Mempulwatnu, lir Melai niwra nsumbain la Itmatromlawanni.
source_text: Then he went to the back of the boat and early in the morning when the first red rays appeared in the east he called to God, in Malay they call this 'praying to the Lord'.

target_text: Na'ul lia watu maka rara werta puou id na'nama ntania la heyanan na'nima npollia Uplerlawna: "Ei Matromlawnu na, Uplerlawna Mempulwatnu, dodo'on di de aupuolu-wuak ti o'a, mhueri tlinmu-mutatar matmu, mutlina-mutailia ali'ru-atu'nu, polpuo'lu-wakwa'ku.
source_text: He picked up a rock which was in the boat, and he offered it up to heaven then called on God. "Oh God, the Almighty, now I am asking you, turn your head and eyes to listen to my words and my request.

target_text: Dodo'on di de ailia'awa wuwulla hletna tpopioini-yoiri kdieldelma.
source_text: Now I am going into the deepest sea.

target_text: A'uwilu-uwala wat di la a' ino'nu.
source_text: Consider/compare this rock as/to my body.

target_text: La lla'pa muyori-mudari a'u pa a'uti'ila-uwal die, de wat di a'utretnia la tah'i de npali.
source_text: If you will protect me and allow me to return, let this rock I throw into the water float.

target_text: Mere ailia lla'pa muati-muolu ahgo'a-tiawu de muala pa wat di nteprernu.
source_text: But if I will die in the sea then cause this rock to sink.

target_text: Dewade de natrerun watu la tah'i de watu npali.
source_text: Then he dropped the rock into the water, and the rock floated.

target_text: Noka na'ala pa lokr owa'ana: "Ei Matromlawnu na aupuolu owa'ana awuak owa'ana ti o'a, plola lla'pa amuati-muolu hgo'a-tiaw la hletan di wikni-yoir di ralamni de wat di mana natniepar wehl ihi nadguaur watu metma.
source_text: Then he took it again and earnestly prayed, "Oh God, I am asking you again, if it is true that I will die in the sea then let this rock sink like the steel of a machete or a black rock.

target_text: Mere lla' pa muormiori-diardiari mhimpai-mmuahatg a'u pa a'uti'ili-uwallia a noh'u-a rai'yu de wat di npali.
source_text: But if I will live, and you will protect me and allow me to return to my land then let this rock float."

target_text: Noka natrernu owa'ana watu de, watu npali owa'ana.
source_text: Then he let the rock drop again, and again it floated.

target_text: Dewade na' owan la watu pa llokarnana re'eni wotelu emak had owa'ana.
source_text: Then he took the rock again for a third time and did like that again (that is, prayed the same earnest prayer).

target_text: Dewade natrernu de watu npali.
source_text: He let the rock drop (again), and it floated.

target_text: Watu npaliwa dewade e' mana lelmerun wali wa.
source_text: After the rock floated (again) he dove into the water.

target_text: Nwuwlierun la tah'i de de ed olek la nu'nu id tutnu.
source_text: He descended into the sea and he came to a banyan tree.

target_text: Dewade nlol nu'nu la yaw pa lla la' de de happe'a ida natentieninreri la nu'nu nainni.
source_text: He went below the tree and saw an old woman busily weaving under the banyan tree.

target_text: Lla'awa noka nwaka kalwieda la happe'a noka happe'a niwra: "Up ei, omdiella meni? O ma mhi'a hya'a?"
source_text: He went and greeted the old woman. The woman said, "Where are you coming from? What are you doing?"

target_text: "Ulala upa."
source_text: (He answered), "I'm just traveling around, grandmother."

target_text: Noka rror rwahaur-wahaur noka nakotla upni di: "Upa, edon mutlin hadoma ntuini la handi na, rokat la handi na?"
source_text: Then the two of them talked and talked, and finally he asked the old woman, "Did you hear anything fall down here?"

target_text: Noka niwra: "Upa a' ge don umkek hadoma, a'u tlin to'a hadoma rokat la kurna hiwi yaterun genni mlia mukekteka, yana etla ma hiwi nernu olekwa."
source_text: Then she said, "I did not see anything, but I heard a noise by the chicken's nest. Go have a look. Maybe what you are seeking is there because the chicken has already come down."

target_text: Noka lla la' de namkeknana prahni la kurna, noka na'ala pa niwra: "Upa ed olek di wa.
source_text: Then he went and saw the ax head in the nest. Then he took it and said, "Grandmother, here it is."

target_text: Prahni pa ailiernana oleka."
source_text: I have found the ax head."

target_text: Noka na'ala pa nkenia la warni wuwannu la'a hniekru ralamni.
source_text: Then he picked up the ax head and put it in his loin cloth.

target_text: Nora upni rwahauru-rwahauru noka nakotiwra: "Upa augiwra lia'awa."
source_text: Then he continued to talk with the old woman. After a while he said, "I have to go now."

target_text: Noma upni niwra: "Omlia'awa mere mpei pa apuoltieka i'ina-ya'ana rpa autianteka ha meni maka kwayop pa kottyarg o'o la de."
source_text: The grandmother said, "You can go, but wait for me to call all the fish so I can ask which one will take you back."

target_text: Npolu i'ina-ya'ana, i'ina-ya'ana dom demade riwra: "Ami edonna mla heyanna, mla mloi mla mpali."
source_text: She called many different kinds of fish and they said, "We do not go to the surface of the water."

target_text: Noka npolga ruini, ruini niwra: "Au ge dona lia puali ma'ata."
source_text: She called the sea cow, and the sea cow said, "I do not swim on the surface."

target_text: Npolu iwu, iwu niwra: "Aug edona lia lioi lia puali ma'ta la heyanna, ma a'utlina hruilarna niwra lla heyanna pa mpuolga pa mutianteka."
source_text: Then she called the shark, and the shark said, "I do not travel along the surface of the water, but I heard the sailfish say that he swims on top, call him and ask him."

target_text: Noka npolga hruilarna pa nmai noka natiana: "O miwra mlia heyanna?"
source_text: Then she called the sailfish. When he came she asked, "Do you like to go along the surface?"

target_text: Noka hruilarna niwra: "Yowa, augiwra lia lioi-puallia la heyanna."
source_text: The sailfish said, "Yes, I go along the surface of the water."

target_text: "Mlia mlioi-mpuallia heyanan demade muora muanke' dilla.
source_text: (She said to the sailfish), "You go along the surface with this man."

target_text: La lla'pa mhimpai-muanatga pa mlia lla' pa muottiarga la nohoni-raini.
source_text: You take care of him and bring him safely to his home.

target_text: Omlia la' de nakota hya'a de omliernohora, omliernohora lirni maka ha nakot o'oa ma mhimpai-muanatga eda di totpena nmormiori-ndardiar pa lla'awa nohoni-raini."
source_text: You go and obey whatever he says, bring him home safe and sound."

target_text: Noka nawliohortarga happe'a pa nha'atla hruilarna du'urnu wawannu pa hruilarna nodia pa nma npalwia.
source_text: Then the younger brother said good-bye to the old woman and got on the back of the sailfish and the sailfish carried him away.

target_text: Ne happe' di nwawa Rahrurmetma-Rarlelkialwa.
source_text: This old woman's name was Rarhurmetma-Rarlelkialwa.

target_text: Noka Hruilarna nora Rettiau Ru'ru rpallia tah'i ulti de rma rpallia Railawan nora Yotwawa rletni.
source_text: The sailfish and Rettiau Ruru sailed on top of the water between Timor and Kisar Islands.

target_text: Pa rpallia noha rletni dewade hruilarna napallia Tranan pa ntena rurni-laini la'a Railawna walli Tipru pa nteretia tutnu pa npandoin la pa tutnu de nwawa Nohmehi.
source_text: When they were between the two islands the sailfish faced south to try and see if he had enough power and strength to tear apart the east end of the island of Timor named Nohmeni.

target_text: De hruilarna nten rurni la eda de.
source_text: The sailfish used his strength to do that.

target_text: Noka nwali doini pa nnehna Yotwaw pa de Yotwawa ndiwdiwra pede Yotwawa wo'orni ndella walliwalli na leta etla noha letgarni.
source_text: He turned around and faced/headed toward Kisar Island, and so Kisar shook. Because of this Kisar's mountains are at the edge of the island and the villages are in the middle.

target_text: Noka nnehna Ra'i wia pa lla'awa Romna-Wiatan della pa nweyat la Romna walli warta pa Nohyata Roman dewade nwalidoinia la pa nmaiwa Nohaumetam pa nhi'doinia Nohaumetam pa nweyat la Roman pa nmaiwa Maupor wa pa ntereti Roman.
source_text: Then the sailfish headed north to go to Roma Island to destroy the west side of Roma. The result of this is the island of Nohyata. Then he turned around and came to Nohaumetam to finish it off. Finally he came to Maupor to violently attack Roma.

target_text: Dewade Rettiau Ru'ru nakotla: "Hadewa."
source_text: Then Rettiau Ruru said, "That is enough."

target_text: Hadi edonna.
source_text: Do not destroy this one."

target_text: "Itnehnateka Tranna."
source_text: "Let us just go south."

target_text: Noka rnehna Tranan de rmaiwa Leti wa.
source_text: Then they went south and came to the island of Leti.

target_text: Rmaiwa Leti wa dewade de Rettiau Ru'ru niwra: "Aitia'a eda di."
source_text: When they got to Leti Rettiau Ruru said, "No, not this one."

target_text: Noka Leti ramta'at pa Leti riwra: "Yana mpueyat noh di na nanpena mpei-mnara Lgona upni Lgona a'nani pa rmai nanpena amdudni i'ina ma mpoknihi tgo'a la."
source_text: The (people of) Leti were afraid and said, "Do not destroy us, wait, when Luang people come here we will serve them fish and cider."

target_text: Pede noha di nwawa Tun i'ina Kalorni yoma ndudni 'ina-nwoknihi tgo'a, riwra kalura.
source_text: So this island was named Tun i'ina Kalorni because they cut up fish and poured palm cider which they call kalura.

target_text: Leti riwra rkalura de ita'ana i'in matmata pa ita talla temna tgo'a.
source_text: When Leti people say rkalura it means they eat raw fish while drinking palm cider.

target_text: Noka rrora rmaiwa pa rlol Mo'a noma Rettiau Ru'ru niwra: "Aitia eda di."
source_text: Then the two of them went by the island of Moa and Rettiau Ruru said, "No, not this one."

target_text: Noka rmaiwa Lakur de Lakru namta'ata pa nru'u la yawa pede Lakur nakleha wo'ora-kawru ne rai mtatanni.
source_text: Then they came to Lakor Island. Lakor was so afraid that it looked down so as a result the island of Lakor (today) has no mountains.

target_text: Noka Rettiau Ru'ru niwra: "Itnehna Ra'i."
source_text: Then Rettiau Ruru said, "Let us head north."

target_text: Noka rnehna Ra'i wa pa rokur Dam pa.
source_text: Then they went north heading toward Damar island.

target_text: Rla'awa Dam pa dewade nweyat la Dam pa.
source_text: They went to Damar and caused destruction there.

target_text: Dewade Rettiau Ru'ru niwra: "Hadewa, ma Lgona atia'a hadi."
source_text: Then Rettiau Ruru said, "That is enough, this is not my island."

target_text: Noka rnehna Tranan wa.
source_text: Then they headed south.

target_text: Rnehna Tranan pa rmaiwa dewade Rettiau Ru'ru niwra: "Anoh'u eda de inahati.
source_text: They headed south and came (to the island of Luang) and Rettiau Ruru said, "This is my own home."

target_text: Mupnial lia handi na na agerun pa ailia umkeka u'pu."
source_text: Harbor here so I can get down and go see my grandmother."

target_text: Nmaiwa.
source_text: He came.

target_text: Nmaiwa mel di wa pa nma lla'a nkorkora upni hniarni noka upni niwra: “He' o'a riy'u nei, u'upu nmati nmolu olek la hletan lawan pa yana mmiai pa mpiutra-mpialka a'u.”
source_text: When it was night he went and knocked on his grandmother's door and she said, “Who are you? My grandchild died in the deep sea so do not come and try to deceive me."

target_text: Noka upni (Rettiau Ru’ru) nakotla niwra: “Upa a'ge hadi la, a' inahati pa amwaiwa pa mhwari hniari.”
source_text: Then the grandson (Rettiau Ru’ru) said to her, “Grandma, it is I. It is really true that I have come back, so you can open the door."

target_text: Noka upni nhari hniari pa lla'awa rialam pa.
source_text: Then the grandmother opened the door and let him in.

target_text: Noka nwahaurnohora la upni niwra emkadi-emkadi rtota-rwudi a'u pa emkadina-emkadina, nwahaurnohora.
source_text: Then he talked all about how he had been deceived in various ways.

target_text: Noka niwra: “Erla meni upe?"
source_text: Then he asked, “Grandmother, where are they?""

target_text: Noka upni niwra: “Rrora rmehlim pa e rawoka mak kmehlima.
source_text: His grandmother said, “They are getting married and they were gathering for the wedding party."

target_text: Mel di e rawoka- raleʼega ra."
source_text: This very night they are gathering for it.”

target_text: Noka Rettiau Ru’ru niwra: “Upa mua'ala a kdie'lu di pa mukdielia pa modi mlia llaʼpa mtiot pa mpuikir wa'du."
source_text: Then Rettiau Ruru said, “Grandmother, you take my ring and wear it and go to peel the wa'du, (home made candle)."

target_text: Yoma ululu de edonna rnair lampu rhi' to'a wa'du, rhi’a wa'du wniewra.
source_text: Because a long time ago they did not have lamps, they just used something called wa'du. They made twisted wa'du.

target_text: Kohapio'o la, waʼdu riawna pa rtuʼtua pena rala peli rawah'a pena rtu’tu rwewra la ora-au nanpena rtutnia.
source_text: They took) kusambi seeds, castor oil plants and pounded that together then mixed it with kapok. Then it was pounded some more before twisting it all together around bamboo or wood then it was lit.

target_text: Rtutnia pa riy rla' demade rwikri-rwikria ha' idni imanni.
source_text: They lit it and that( the coil) was peeled open to clean out the ashes.

target_text: Pa happe'a lla la'pa ntotpa nwikirwa’du imanni la patke' di gaini.
source_text: So the old woman went to peel the wa'du in front of the girl (younger brother's wife about to marry older brother).

target_text: Totpena okarni maka kdieli hande la di nalla nwikir wa'du totpena patkeʼa namkeknana kdieli.
source_text: The finger which the ring was on she used to peel the wa'du so the girl (younger brother's wife now marrying older brother) would see the ring.

target_text: Noka happe'a lla'awa.
source_text: The old woman went.

target_text: Lla la'pa natiak wa’du wnikarni la patke' di gaini.
source_text: She went to keep the wa'du burning in front of the girl.

target_text: Noka patke' di namkeka nana kdieli dewade nwarora niwra: “A kdie'lu hadile."
source_text: Then the girl saw the ring and thought, “That is my ring.””

target_text: Mere edon nakota hadoma na nruʼuwa.
source_text: But she did not say anything, she only bowed her head.

target_text: Pena happe’a nwikri wa'du pena patke'a namkek nana kdieli demade nruʼuwa.
source_text: Then the old woman peeled the wa’du. The girl saw the ring but only bowed her head.

target_text: Emkade mammain nek pa reʼeni wotelu ma ha noka edon nakota hadom pwali noka happeʼa nmaiwa.
source_text: This happened three times and she never said anything. Then the old woman came back.

target_text: Happe'a nmai pa nakotla upni dewade upni natiana: "Emkameni up e?"
source_text: The old woman came back to talk to her grandchild. When she arrived home he asked her, "How did it go, grandmother?"

target_text: "Up ei ailia lla' pa awikir wa'du pa namkek toto'a kdie'lu mere nru'u, edonna nakot hadom pali na re'eni wotel noka amuaiwa.
source_text: "Hey, Grandson, I went and peeled the wa'du, but she just looked and bowed her head and said nothing. This happened three times and then I came home."

target_text: Edon nakot hadoma, up ei ha nhoratdoini olek o'o wa.
source_text: "She did not say anything. She has already forgotten you,"

target_text: Yoma nora makre'a-maktaru rmehlima-rmarya'a pa nhoratdoini olek o'a la pa yana mhoratrer neka wa."
source_text: "because she is going to marry a wealthy man."

target_text: Noka Rettiau Ru'ru niwra: "Upa ailia'awa.
source_text: 'Then Rettiau Ruru said, "I'm going."

target_text: Ailia'awa na pena mukekrer nek la wa."
source_text: "Later you will see what will happen."

target_text: Noka nmaiwa pa nha'atla hrui wawannu na'nama nakotla hrui niwra: "Dodo'on di de mtierieti noh dilla.
source_text: 'Then he went and got on the sailfish and said to him, "Now you can cut apart this island."

target_text: Mpeyata-mpuaniawua noh di totpena noh di kukku'a-kekke'a loloha-tawtiawua, yana ntul kotni yana nwaw nanni.
source_text: "Destroy this island so that it is small and not proud."

target_text: Mpeyata-mpuaniaw meman noh dilla."
source_text: "Destroy this island!"

target_text: Noka hrui nakotla: "Had emkade de mtiorer pitpitu.
source_text: 'Then the sailfish said, "If that is the way you want it, hold on tight!"'

target_text: Muawurrer pitpitga a'u me totpena auweyat noh di."
source_text: "Hold on tight so I can destroy the island."

target_text: Dewade ntorer pitpitu hrui du'urnu wawannu na'nama nterwa.
source_text: 'Then he held tightly to the sailfish's back and the sailfish took off leaping into the air.'

target_text: Nterwa dewade nalla Metutnu pa nalla Dona Liakra pa nalla Hawna, Kpuri Ttiata dewade Lgon di rruru.
source_text: 'He shot off hitting Metutnu then Dona, Liakra, Hawna, Kpuri and Tiata. Luang shook violently!'

target_text: Rrur pa riy honnona ramta'at pa rawkikni-raplialin mommuou wa.
source_text: 'When it shook, all the people were so afraid that they all fled and went to other islands.'

target_text: Rtikildoinia-rhaldoinia noh dilla pa makla'awa Herna, makla'awa Papu'a, makla'awa noh paheli rai pa tatra re honnona pa noh di nahgali wa.
source_text: 'Some went as far away as Seram and Papua, while others went to neighboring islands so that the island of Luang was deserted.'

target_text: Ne upni mana namta'at wal wia.
source_text: 'The grandmother was also afraid.'

target_text: Upni niwra: "Idei u'upnu hihi'ini-yapyapni hadi, hota nweyat noh di, pa ailia wuahaka."
source_text: 'She said, "Oh no, this is my grandchild's doing. He is going to ruin this island. I will go and find him."

target_text: Noka upni nerunwa.
source_text: 'Then his grandmother went down (to the shore).'

target_text: Upni nerun pa la'awa Gain Tutnu dewade de hrui mana nter pa nnehn oleka Tranan pa nawalia pa niwra napallia Tia'ata totpena ntereti owa'ana Ttia'ata demade nal owa'an la Nohinni.
source_text: 'She went to the beach and headed towards Gain Tutnu. Then the sailfish took off heading south and turned to face Tiata in order to break apart Tiata and then take on Nohinni.'

target_text: Dewade upni ed olek la Gain Tutnu.
source_text: 'The his grandmother was already at Gain Tutnu.'

target_text: Pa hrui niwra nti'ila pa napali Ttia'at wa dewade de nanaur pa nwak lili-maumuau la upa hrui pa nadia'du pa npollia upa hrui niwra:
source_text: The sailfish turned around to face Tiata. (The grandmother) was chewing betel nut and she pleaded to the sailfish for help. To stop him from destroying the island, she called to him (singing this song):

target_text: Wawaw rara Surriai, awuaw raraoo Surriai ei,
source_text: My name is Lady Surriai, eh

target_text: Aweda rara Lelriai,
source_text: My name is Miss Lelriai, ne'

target_text: Awuaw rara Surriai, ma upriri oo liltutnu ei,
source_text: My name is Lady Surriai, come to stand on the shore's tip, eh,

target_text: Aweda rara Lelriai, ma ukded la Ilgaini ne,
source_text: My name is Miss Lelriai, come right up to the point, ne;

target_text: Ма upriri lia Iltutnu, polpolu up oo srui ei,
source_text: I come right up to the edge of the sand to ask a favor of grandfather sailfish, eh,

target_text: Ma ukded la Ilgaini wuakwak a’na awalana ne,
source_text: I come right up to the edge of the sand to ask a favor of the fish's child, ne;

target_text: Polpolu upa u srui, yana mpue oo yat noh ei,
source_text: I ask of grandfather sailfish, do not destroy this island, eh,

target_text: Wuawak ana wlana'a, yana mpuaniawu rai ne,
source_text: I ask of the moon's child, do not crush the world, ne;

target_text: Yana mpue yat noha, mkeitar tutnu oo id ei,
source_text: Do not destroy this island, leave one end, eh,

target_text: Yana mpuaniawu rai, maltary laini ida ne,
source_text: Do not crush the world, leave a small sliver, ne;

target_text: Mkeitar tutnu ida, tutnu id oo pa hgol ie,
source_text: Leave one end for me to stay, eh,

target_text: Maltaru laini ida, laini id pa yleta ne,
source_text: Leave one strip for me to live, ne;

target_text: Wawaw rara Surriai,
source_text: My name is Lady Surriai, eh,

target_text: Aweda rara Lelriai ne,
source_text: My name is Miss Lelriai, ne.

target_text: Dewade naldoini knamni la wawni ralamni pa nnaklu la upa hrui wa dewade upa hrui nkeranwa happe'a mana nkeran wal wia pa nwallia watu pa etla Gain Tutnu de nru’rer lia yawa.
source_text: Then she took out a piece of betel nut from her mouth and threw it at the sailfish. Then both she and the sailfish turned to stone. She is there till this day still bowing her head.

target_text: Nhoruwa.
source_text: The End.

target_text: Anni ida, patke’a nanni Oktovina nora kakni muanke’a a’nani patkeʼa lawna woru, ri’ida nanni Mina, ri'ida nanni Jakomina, muankeʼa ida wali nanni Godtlifa.
source_text: One year, there was a woman named Oktovina and her male siblings two grownup female children, one named Mina, one named Jakomina, and also a male named Godtlifa.

target_text: Godtlifde, Oktovina a'nani gari pa la'a rerunla rwahaka krita la Lailiawna, Tamta onni.
source_text: This Godtlifa, was Oktovina's youngest child and so they went to sea to look for octopus at Lailiawna.

target_text: Rla'wa la'a Lailiawna dewede inni Oktovina nora patke'a rrora rerunla.
source_text: They went to Lailiawna then mother Oktovina and those two girls got down (off the boat).

target_text: Rerunla Lailiawna pa irwotelu rwahaka krita.
source_text: They got off at Lailiawna and the three of them searched for octopus.

target_text: Ir'rhopna Godtlifa te'ena loi pa nalaullia Tamta.
source_text: They told Godtlifa to pole the canoe, to go ahead of them to Tamta.

target_text: Irwotelu tepartarlia krita wnyahakni dewede metimana napra.
source_text: The three of them were absorbed in the search for octopus then the tide also began to rise.

target_text: Lerdede irwotelu lernana krita liawanni dewede irwotelu rahlera krita la keranni.
source_text: On that day the three of them had gotten many octopus, then the three of them threw their octopus on the land.

target_text: Tepartarlia yala'a dewede wauwau nmaide merannidi nokru Upahrui.
source_text: They were in the process of walking when the current came with great strength heading for Upahrui.

target_text: Irwotelu ta'eni thannana wauwau dewede irhoplia la krita makra'enniana hanona.
source_text: The three of them could not stand against the tide, then they threw away all the octopus which they had gotten.

target_text: Irwotelu rnanlia Upahrui mera lerdede inni Oktovina nora Mina ta'eni rnanniana.
source_text: The three of them swam for Upahrui but at that time mother Oktovina and Mina could not swim.

target_text: Dewede inni Oktovina nora Mina teprerunla tah'i mera Jakomina narurlia niani pa lernana Upahrui la keranni.
source_text: Then mother Oktovina and Mina sank into the sea but Jakomina was strong at swimming and got to the land at Upahrui.

target_text: Noka na'ala aranni samomou dewede nha'atla tutuwawannu mera donna namkekanana ra.
source_text: Then she took a good breath then climbed up to the top but she could not see them.

target_text: Ir'rora rteprernu olekwa dewede Jakomina nkakurwa, nhawnu, yoma inni Oktovina nora Mina rmati olekwa.
source_text: The two of them had already drowned then Jakomina cried, and shouted because her mother Oktovina and Mina had already died.

target_text: Lerdede puou, loi, idmana edonna rlereti, noma leramana nheriawa.
source_text: That day not even one boat or canoe passed by, then the sun also set.

target_text: Lerdede Godtlifa maka kte'ennana loi pa nalaullia, naplingeti inni nora Mina rmatia olekwa.
source_text: That day Godtlifa who had poled the canoe to go ahead of them, did not even know that his mother and Mina had already died.

target_text: Lera ntuini dewede muanke'a ida nanni Timotius la'a Tamta.
source_text: At sun down then one man named Timotius went to Tamta.

target_text: Tepartarlia ntie'ena dewede inni Oktovina moratnu nmanaknyuinla te'ena.
source_text: He was in the process of poling his canoe then mother Oktovina's hair became entangled around his pole.

target_text: Yei Timotius nheduma, namkeka rimatidi pa naknyaunanade inni Oktovina.
source_text: Uncle Timotius was shocked, seeing this dead person so he yelled, “Mother Oktovina.”

target_text: Dewede nkawi la loi makla'a Tamta pa rmara'ala inni Oktovina pa rodia la'a leta.
source_text: Then he motioned to the canoes that went to Tamta to come and get mother Oktovina and bring her to the village.

target_text: Rla'wa letade, makdella leta rheduma.
source_text: When they went to the village, those in the village we shocked.

target_text: Inni narni rpolu, rkakru pa rmarala, rodi inni Oktovina la roma nayanni.
source_text: The relatives were called, they cried for them to come get her, and bring mother Oktovina to the house.

target_text: Paprai nhopna limarora la'a rwahaka kekenkua rwotelu, yanpa rmati olekwa.
source_text: The village chief ordered the people to go search for those three children, hopefully they had not already died.

target_text: Rwahakneka pa makla'a Tamta, Upahrui, Hawna.
source_text: They just kept searching so some went to Tamta, to Upahrui, and to Hawna.

target_text: Makla’a Upahrui wakriani keranni, Jakomina namkeknana dewede npolu pa marala.
source_text: When those that went to Upahrui came close to the shore, Jakomina saw them then called them to come get her.

target_text: Maralade nkakrunande, noka iratiana Godtlifa nora Mina erlameni?
source_text: When they came and got her she was crying and crying, then they asked, "Where are Godtlifa and Mina?"

target_text: Noka Jakomina nakotniwra Godtlifa etla Tamta, Mina nora inni Oktovina ta’eni rnanni pa irrora rmati olekwa.
source_text: Then Jakomina said, "Godtlifa is at Tamta, Mina and mother Oktovina could not swim so they already died."

target_text: Noka maklakala Jakomina rakotniwra inni Oktovina lernana olekwa.
source_text: Then those that went to get Jakomina said that they already found mother Oktovina.

target_text: Noka irodia Jakomina pa maila'a leta.
source_text: Then they brought Jakomina and came to the village.

target_text: Rmai la leta dewede iralernu Jakomina noka rawalio wa'ana pa la rwahaka Mina.
source_text: They came to the village, then they let Jakomina down then they returned again to search for Mina.

target_text: Irte'ena pa rokru Tamta.
source_text: They used a pole to push their boat toward Tamta.

target_text: Limarora makla’a Tamta rodia oleka Godtlifa me limarora makla’a Hawna, Kpuri.
source_text: The people who went to Tamta already brought Godtlifa and the people who went to Hawna and Kpuri.

target_text: Tepartarlia wnyahaka mera ira edonna lernanetia.
source_text: They were in the process of searching but they still had not found anything.

target_text: Noka ira walpia rmaiwia leta.
source_text: Then they returned back to the village.

target_text: Repardoin yawyawra ma’ata, rhakretia limarora makwarini pa rtamin mati (inni Oktovina), makla’a rwahaka Mina.
source_text: Early the next morning, they divided the people; those to stay behind to bury the dead (mother Oktovina), and those to go search for Mina.

target_text: Irwahaknekpa normar lera owa’ana.
source_text: They just kept searching till the sun set again.

target_text: Dewede makdella Tamta irmai eniwawanu noka ramkekde (Mina) nanyewa la eniwawanu.
source_text: Then those who were at Tamta came to the beach then they saw that (Mina) was rolling on the beach.

target_text: Noka irala pa rkenia la loi rodia maila'a leta (Lgona).
source_text: Then they got her and put her in the canoe to bring her to the village (Luang).

target_text: Rmaila leta, irayapi lumni pleta pleta pa irla’a rtamni yoma nahuwu olekwa.
source_text: When they came to the village, they made a coffin in order to quickly bury her because she already smelled.

target_text: Hare matmiatni lerdede inni narni rsusdoinla.
source_text: The relatives were extremely distressed by the tragedy on that day.

target_text: Yahoamde Godtlifa nora Jakomina rkakru lelera melmela.
source_text: What is more, Godtlifa and Jakomina cried day and night.

target_text: Nhorwa.
source_text: Finished

target_text: Ei, Matromlawnu ne, Orgahi Orha'a, Uplerlawna Mempulwatnu.
source_text: Oh, our Lord, Lord God.

target_text: O'etla gentutulu-watliolo'ona, Ilwio'itu-Darwonema, Ilyamou Watyatoha.
source_text: You are in the highest, in Heaven.

target_text: Mere dodo'ondi de, aghoi lia kotmu-awetla nanmu, apualu-wuak tiy O'a, ghoi idma rrama lia'ara, totpena muheri tlinmu-mutatar matmu, mutlina-mutaili, mlina-muata reria ami lia noh kerna-rai kieran di wawannu.
source_text: But now, I say your name, I pray to you, I worship you in order that you will listen and see us who are on this earth.

target_text: Apuolu-awuak tiy O'a totpena mhilpai-muanatu, muhlili-mulakma, muyori-mudari ami lia riy ornoha-orrai di.
source_text: I pray to you in order that you take care of and watch over us on this earth.

target_text: Mudopardoini-muhaldoini nyeni-nyhena, rinni-kniahra maiya ami.
source_text: Take away disease and plagues from us.

target_text: Mitieridoini-muhaldoini yotyotni-yatyatni maiya ami.
source_text: Take away evil from us.

target_text: Muala amormior mamni pa nawerna-naplahwa, ammorniana a tup mamni, amlawannana a liawan mamni, la'pa amlerla mto'a-ppe'a nihtuini-mortihamra, lli'ina ndahla-awu npo'pa nanpena Orgahi-Orha'a mhoi lia mkot mamni-mpetla a nan mamni mtieman la a lim mamni miriyhamilla a dopal mamni.
source_text: Give us long life so that we will live a long time until we are old with white teeth and fallen teeth, then God will come and call our name.

target_text: Ampolu-ampak tiy O'a totpena mhilpai-muanatga a' in mamni nar mamni, a' am mamni hyali miamni la'a a noh mamni raiy miamni, totpena lera idpa am idma nwatroma-ntahnei id de, ama'uli mawedi reria o kotmu-o-nanmu.
source_text: We pray to you in order that you take care of our relatives on this earth of ours, so that on the day we meet each other we will praise your name.

target_text: Mho'doini-mhaidoini a do' mamni-hal mamni.
source_text: Erase our sins.

target_text: Polpuolu mamni-wakwak mamni di de amheli-mpapna he' dilla a'namu Wutmeha-Laimieha.
source_text: This prayer of ours we are connecting to the one whose name is the one and only heir/son.

target_text: Totto'a (Amin).
source_text: True.

target_text: Ina-ama, Ina-nara, makle'lu-makdalwa.
source_text: Respected elders and relatives, those who are gathered around.

target_text: La' lera Orgahi-Orha'a Uplerlawna Mempulwatnu Nakoki-nayapia, Nakoma-napala, Nhedruh'a-ntaplihi it upni-tgarni Wuwtian wioka-Lai tian miera nora Ruh meh inni-Uh mueh riwni.
source_text: At one time the Lord God created, formed, put together our ancestors Adam [lit. gathered dustgathered red clay] and Eve [lit. one rib only mother-only rib].

target_text: Nhornioma Ntera-ndema la kalwiedni-paitiotni.
source_text: Then he took care of them with peace and blessings on every side.

target_text: Wuwtian wioka-Lai-tian miera nora ulwualli-tnialwialli de rmori-rdarlia il wiyo'riwnu-gen wio'mara.
source_text: Adam and partner/pair (Eve) lived in paradise.

target_text: La' noma hegana amlawanni ralamni namehra la it upni-tgarni rrora rmori-rdarlia pripanni-fa'anni ralamni.
source_text: Then the devil was jealous/angry at our two ancestors who were living in blessedness.

target_text: Noma hegana nawiru-nawalia inonnila Tok mier wu'u-Ni' mar rahlu pa nodia nur siawortra-namsale'u la Ruh meh inni-Uh mueh riwni.
source_text: Then the devil turned his body into a snake (lit. reptile red spying-snake yellow) in order to bring deceit to Eve (lit. one rib only mother-only rib).

target_text: Noma nwotra-le'niana Wuwtian wioka-Lay tian miera pede rlerla matmiati-molmuolu hoho'a-tawtiawu la'pa ralumni rakietra la Up rar noha-Rar rayi nora kodni awnu-topni-tanni owa'ana.
source_text: Then he deceived Adam so that they received death which resulted even in being buried in the earth and becoming dust again.

target_text: La'pa it upni-tgarni yatotni-yarieini emkade ho'mana, Orgahi-Orha'a edona Nolin lima-nwe'er-rorni la Wuw tian wioka-Lai tian miera kotnu-turnu gerni-wniaunu.
source_text: Even though our ancestors were tempted like that, God did not stop taking care of Adam's descendants (Lit seminal fluid water-exchange).

target_text: La'pa Kain nkaklia po'a-liwra manga garni Habel pa nok rara-nwaltie'eni.
source_text: Time went on till Kain hit very hard Habel till he died (lit. blood came out-turn into feces).

target_text: La'pa Habela aranni naprir niohora tniunu hniaranni-odawni la'pa natipu-natnian lia Orgahi-Orha'a Uplerlawna-Mempulwatnu makdenla Ilwo'itu-Darwionema, Ilyamou-Watyatoha.
source_text: Then Habela's sacrificed life (death) was a witness crying out to the Lord God who lives in heaven (lit. One who owns all, the great grandfather sun the most precious jewel/stone who dwells at the sixth or seventh level on the pure mountain/land-set apart rock).

target_text: Noma Orgahi-Orha'a Uplerlawna Mempulwatnu Ndi'na Kain yeheni-lowa Kain hlorni.
source_text: Then the Lord God sent Kain away for good [lit. completely washed out Kain's footsteps.

target_text: Mere la'pa Kain nwaktarlia pa lergotwa noma Uplerlawna nhonnia Kain reranni.
source_text: But when Kain was about to leave then God put a sign on Kain's forehead.

target_text: Puka lirni enakota de Uplerlawna edona nhortaplinga lir mak ha nakota.
source_text: The book/Bible says that God does not forget the words/promise he has said/made.

target_text: Nomlerni de enakota la'a Wuwtian wioka-Lai tian miera niwra: Mi'upa-mi'a'na totpena mipenga noh di wawannu.
source_text: Long ago he said to Adam: "Bear children and fill the earth."

target_text: Mere la'pa rimormiori re rpeh mutliawna-rlawan ketiaru, noma kleh ya'unna-yamta'ata la Uplerlawna-Mempulwatnu pa la'pa nte'ela Up Nuh tuwnu.
source_text: But when those people multiplied, then they did not have respect for God until it reached until Noah's time.

target_text: Noma Orgahi-Orha'a Uplerlawna ritie'era lyanti pa ger otna naktiowru me nha'apre'era noh marna pa ger ormata roplia riwriwu-hararna.
source_text: Then the Lord God split apart the heavens so rain fell down and stepped on the earth so the springs of water would flow.

target_text: Noma narieniande rimormiori rlerla kowlora-pah'a meti.
source_text: Then he caused people to reach to destruction.

target_text: Mere Uplerlawna orgahani sniayanni pa Nala konkona-aupuali na nalewna Nuh nor hawni-a'nani.
source_text: But because of God's own love therefore he took a boat to save Noh and his wife and children.

target_text: Rimormioria riwnu-halli re enekneka Orgahi-Orha'a ntawdioinia rimormiori re wo'awa pa rtikilrerlia yehtan miera me rhaparrerlia hlor wewnihi.
source_text: The multitudes of people (were not saved) except God set apart those eight people to walk along the right path/path of righteousness.

target_text: Mere la'pa emkade ho'mana rimormiori rpeh mutliawna-rlawan keitiarwua.
source_text: But even though it was like that people increased in number and multiplied.

target_text: Noma kleh ya'unna-yamta'at la Uplerlawna lirNi-tunNu.
source_text: Then they lacked respect for God's words.

target_text: Uplerlawna orgahani Nal limni nantoreri lirNi-tunNu deulLu-tatarNi maka kahniorattarlia watu le'u pa Nala la Musa pa totpena itamkek memna mere yeher to'ame do'a-hala naitittarrerlia.
source_text: God himself used his hands to hold his law which was written on stone and give to Musa so in order that we can really see (the truth) but all the more greatly sin increased.

target_text: Matialo'onamde Uplerlawna takenia ntahanana.
source_text: Perhaps God could not endure this any longer.

target_text: Noma Nnairia rimormioria makmori-kdarlia tlin tetema-nampulwullu pa rhi'a makwohor ulu-ktatrulu la'a Wutmueha-Lai mieha hota ntopur la maiya noh marna wawannu.
source_text: Then he used people who are uncivilized (lit. people who live all ears and hairy tongue?) to become prophets concerning (the fact that) the One and Only Son/Heir will descend down to this earth.

target_text: La'a Lukas pukni de e nwahaur nohora la lerni ha rtora Yesus la krahana Betlahem.
source_text: In Luke's book it talks about the time that Jesus was born in the Betlahem stable.

target_text: La'pa itatlina lira niwra: rtora, nnia'eratni de rayoria onde rmoria.
source_text: When we hear the words saying, "rtora," its meaning is bear or give life/birth.

target_text: Mere la' pa'etnu de nhi'inde yawala Lgona lir ina-ama riwra: Wutmeha-Lai mieha Ntopurla noh marna wawannu.
source_text: But in the traditional culture in the Luang language of our ancestors they say: The One and Only Son/Heir descends on the earth.

target_text: Emaknekame Lgona ra'aplinga lir maka kiwra: na'nama e rtor papayi id de nwaw Yesus.
source_text: It is as if the Luang people do not know the words like this: just then a baby named Jesus was born.

target_text: Yoma emaknekame Lgona e ratniohor de Yesus maka na'nama ha rayori de, Wutmueha-Laimieha e inhatte.
source_text: Because it is just like Luang people know that the one who was just born, was the true One-and Only Son/Heir of a king.

target_text: Yoma la'a hya'a?
source_text: Why was that?

target_text: Pede Lgona itakot emkadena, de onnila lerni upa-wlada rma rhu'ula ita tlinni-twer it matni, de rala Yesus nanNi me rwatut itla pniaki la puka ralamni de, riwra Yesus di, de rmor hya'dilla Betlahem la' noh makden warta roo!
source_text: We Luang people say this, because in the time of our ancestors the ancestor westerners came and put holes in our earth and opened our eyes, that-is they gave us Yesus' name and they taught us how to read the book, they said this Jesus, he was born in Betlahem on an island in the far west.

target_text: Mere nomlerni, la noha nhera-rayi nwanni, illi npoka-watu npetu, de lir in-ama riwra: hiwi naro'wa pitga terannu la' kuranni, me ahu nayamarlia diadallu.
source_text: But long ago, when the earth was young/newly created, the boulders and rocks were breaking apart, in our ancestors words they would say: the chicken lays strongly its egg in the nest, and dogs are tamed from the chains.

target_text: Itla maiye Lgona-Mdona, Nohlumni-Ray Mietma, Watga'illi-Let Ra' leta, it mori-tdarlia melmellikalkalamni. Mere la'a rima-rima illi-watnu de nu'nu mutu-natar leta er olekla wa.
source_text: We here in Luang (Luang Sermata, Island swallow-Land dark, Rock mountain face Village north?), we lived in darkness. But on every rock there was a banyan tree and a village already.

target_text: Tui nakota de la'a itla Lgon di, de ratu rwatniarla lyanit marna pa rhoilia wunu-rtanlia lera, la roma polwunu-waklera.
source_text: Our history says that concerning us our Luang ancestors knew how to pray (lit. bow to the sky and cry out to the sun and moon), in the praying house.

target_text: Hade edmaka karurnian itla it hnia'argeni, pa itakot nohor walia Wutmueha-Lai mieha ha lollola.
source_text: That is what strengthens us in our position, so that we can also talk about the One-and Only Son's affairs.

target_text: Miai pia tal it yawala Lgonni ta takot nohora Yesus Makamori-kalewan de!
source_text: Come let us use the Luang language to talk about Christ Jesus!

target_text: Emaknekam de Makwohorullu-ktatrulu Mika wniahaurnu yanullu me ntatra yatnianila Samaria me Yerusalem de niwra: Makden nohkerna wawannu honomi mitlina: Orgahi-Orga'a makdenla tutullulolo'oni hota nma Ntutrer wial pia miora mihuri-wiwo'ora.
source_text: Just like the prophet Mika's chapter, "One's crying over Samaria and Yerusalem saying: All of you on earth listen. God who dwells in the highest will come and stand to war with you."

target_text: Tniatar lirni re'eni wotellu de niwra e Nwatiauwua hititni-lomomarni pa Nernu.
source_text: The third verse says that He will come down from glory.

target_text: Lgona ita edon tlernana ma'ta puka lirni, de it upni-tgarni lirni meman la ululu genni, de upa-wlada rodia puka kot kalwieda-paitiot di, de e riwra e rayor oleka Yesus.
source_text: When we Luang people had not yet received the words of the book/Bible, our ancestors of long ago said that when the ancestor westerners brought this book of the good news, they used the words: "Jesus has been already born."

target_text: Mere it yawala Lgonni la wniohor lir maranni de niwra: Wutmueha-Lai mieha ma Ntopru.
source_text: But our Luang language in the traditional language says: The One-and Only Son descends.

target_text: La'pa itaweta tniopru, ha nnia'eratni de, emolmolan neka me itiwra maktopru la aralma.
source_text: When we say descent, it means that, it is like we are talking about descending in battle.

target_text: Ntopru nnia'eratni emakwalime ri'ida ndella heyanan pa nehtiar lia yawa.
source_text: The meaning of 'He descends' is just like a person who is up high and jumps down.

target_text: Puka lirni toto meman pa nod niohor it yawala Lgonni.
source_text: The book/Bible's words truly go along/back up our Luang language.

target_text: It yawalla Lgonni re'ela nwahainiana Uplerlawna lir yade'eni-yamoyanni la'a puka ralamni.
source_text: Our Luang language helps to make clear God's secret/deep words in the book/Bible.

target_text: Itala it yawala Lgonni tatwakerkar wutlia puka ralamni de, emolmolan nekame po'a wnieta.
source_text: Let us use our Luang language to look closely into the book/Bible, just as if we were breaking it open.

target_text: Etla puka ralamni de eniwra: Majus onde lirmelai niwra ahli bintang/astronot, yawala Lgona niwra makodia ukru-rehera, wniohora niwra makatu kakwieta lotielu lipni-rarlimna-laini.
source_text: It is in the book/Bible it says: The Majus or in Malay it says ahli bintang/astronot, the term in the Luang language is: those who do unusual things, in traditional language we say those who can discern the early morning stars.

target_text: Noma la'pa makatu kakwieta lotielu lipni-rarlimna laini rla' pa ratiana Herodes, maktorna lodna-hairi ratiana riwra: "Keke'en maka na'nama ha rayorniande etla me?
source_text: Then when those who discern the early morning stars went to ask Herodes, the one in charge of the kingdom they asked saying: "Where is the child that was just born?'

target_text: Ama matian pa mtiut geni totpa amla'a.
source_text: We come and ask for you to point out the place for us to go (to find Him).'

target_text: Yoma ot E edmaka ktikiltarlia yeh tan miera, me khapar rerlia hlor wewnihi ne E' nanpena edmaka kodi plolli la Yehudi riwnu-halli ri!
source_text: Because He is the one who will go along the right path/path of righteousness and He only is the one who has power over this large number of Yehudi people.

target_text: Herodes niwra: " Age uplin niohora de!
source_text: Herodes said: "I do not know about it!'

target_text: Mere la'pa plola pa etla, de mikot a' tiotpena arie'e la guh idma-riama lia'arni."
source_text: But if He really exists, then you tell me in order that I can worship him."

target_text: Raye Herodes nmeh'a nekade naplinga.
source_text: King Herodes himself did not even know.

target_text: Mere makanina-kamat niohora puka lirni de e ratga yoma la' puka ralamni de ed makakot nohora Mika lirni re'eni wolimni tniatarni yanullu niwra: Hei Betlaham Efrata yapatni, riy riwra o kuku'u-keke'u maiya Yehudi ri letni re.
source_text: But those who really knew the scriptures knew because in the book/Bible it talks about Mika's words in the fifth chapter and first verse saying: Oh Betlahem Efrata area, people say that you are the smallest of the villages in Yehudi.

target_text: Mere hota nwatiau let ku'umu di pa A'u ariana metam keranni idla pa nodi plolli la Israil makatenna ulga let dilla ululu plialiani.
source_text: But later coming from this your small village/area I will raise one who is very great to rule over Israil who came from this village from of old.

target_text: Herodies natlina de namta'ata, yoma makwohor ulu-ktatrulu lirni, ne itmana tamta'at wali yoma it lirni la ululu meman mana, itiwria Wut mueha-Lai mieha nma Ntopru la noh marna, de emakwalime e nahak ya'arni la ri' maka edon kamta'ata Uplerlawna Mempulwatnu lirNi-tunNu.
source_text: When Herodes heard that he was afraid, because of the prophet's words, and we also are also afraid because in our words from the very beginning even, we say the One-and Only Son/Heir of the king will descend to the earth just like he is searching for war with those who do not respect God's Words.

target_text: La'pa itwarora lira-tun muak ha tpaiknana la puka ralamni ri, de yana seslia pa tiwa plinu-plo' nek itla wniarora-wnialiai la Wutmueha-Lai mieha Ntopur la noh kerande wawannu.
source_text: If we think about the words that we have read in the book/Bible, let us not pretend that we do not know about the thinking that the One-and Only Son/Heir will descend on the earth.

target_text: Yoma Enatga de ita maiyi Lgon di, de tlerla yahuri-yawo'ora.
source_text: Because He knows that we here in Luang, are fighting.

target_text: Itiwra Lgon di ed makodia deulu-tatra plola-mneha mere twaldionia de tamat mera-tawul kgaulu pa hota narieiniande it uhwanu mana edona napniarwutlia wirtawi wewerna makokarla lyanti me mur la'a plalahwa maka kwahipnila noha uwarnu.
source_text: We say that this Luang is what carries traditional true law but yet we seize each other's possessions so that later the result will be that will not prosper (lit. our sprouts will not grow into wide leaves which push up for the sky and our roots will not be long and grow deep into the ground).

target_text: Edona twarornana lira puka ralamni niwra Wutmeha-Lai mieha Ntopur de nodia kalwieda-paitiota rhinlel tiutu-relan mahmara yoma Natga de itawlar hal oleka kalwiedni-paitiotni?
source_text: Why are we not thinking about/paying attention to the words in the book/Bible which say the One-and-Only Son/Heir will descend bringing true judgment? He will descend because He knows that we have run away already from peace.

target_text: Twer it matni la a'na riyi patiata Lgona ri.
source_text: Let us pay attention to (the needs of) these widows and orphans (the destitute) here in Luang.

target_text: Yan itwei pia meti nhapenga nanpena itna'aili.
source_text: Let us not wait until full tide before we go fishing (let us not put off helping them).

target_text: Ne emkameni la a'na riyi patiata?
source_text: What about the widows/poor?

target_text: Dari nwewar noha, towa namatia krita-watrora, emkameni la Lgon uhunu riwni polpuolu wakwakni la maktera-kdema, makohi-kara, makawilla-kayomtia.
source_text: Nets are all over the island, traps? are killing octopus and shellfish, how about the many Luang people's cry to the one who cares for people, the Creator and Sustainer?

target_text: Yesus Nmai die nodia kalwiedni pa yan tahuri-tawo'or nohora meti haru.
source_text: Jesus came to bring peace so that we do not argue about harvesting the reef.

target_text: Mutu Mnoa riwa ir metni, Enwiawna riwra ir metni.
source_text: People from West Luang say it is their reef, People from East Luang say it is their reef.

target_text: Upa-tgara rhi' taru-ryaptarg oleka watu niohora autiatra mere tuwuari-laweru rwatutlia matmera wulkgaulu.
source_text: The ancestors already created a boundary, but the young people are learning to seize other possessions.

target_text: Tui nakottarga de Lgona ohorni-Mniet apannu ed makodia rinni-woki maiye Lgona Nohinna-Ray amni di.
source_text: History says that Luang's navel-and Mnietu's stomach are the ones that bring refreshment to Luang (lit. island of our mothers-land of our fathers).

target_text: Mutu Mnioa la'pa rwa'ilga maranni de Enwiawna Mnietu edmaka kpolliohora, mere etla me?
source_text: West Luang, when they agreed traditionally, said that Enwiawna Mnietu are the ones to do the rebuking, but where is it?

target_text: Mutu Mnoa rora Enwiawna riwa rwanatarla metkierna wawannu, de Letupnu edmaka kpolliohora, mere etla me?
source_text: When West Luang and East Luang want to make rules about the reef, it is Letupnu that must rebuke, but where is it?

target_text: La' Amsal wniahaurni re'eni teramporu wehrani woru tatarni teramporu wehrani wo'awa eniwra: Yana mpuatitnia rira tiemni-liannu la'a tan ululu maka ha muplin niohora wniahaurnu la upmu-tgarmu lerni.
source_text: In Psalms chapter twenty-two, verse twenty-eight it says: Do not move a boundary marker from old land concerning which you do not know the discussion from your ancestors time.

target_text: Orgahi-Orha'a Yesus Makamori-kalewna Niwra: Atiopurla nohkerna wawannu, de mimiat niohor A'u yoma mpiata'wa a ge'nu, de lep mutmu-lakpona rpennian A'u pede mliernan alia pip-diuma lowanikrahani.
source_text: The Lord Jesus Christ says: I am descending to the earth, you know about Me because you have searched for My place; the inns were too full for me therefore you found Me in the goat and sheep stable.

target_text: Lirmi-yatmi ukru-rehermi rtutnian alia a i'nu riwni wawannu.
source_text: Your knowledge and insight found me in my mother's lap.

target_text: Rariwa-rahai alia pipi-wawi geni tienni.
source_text: They have placed me in the sheep and goat's place.

target_text: Maktorna krita o'tani me hairi lia wuwannu mana, edona rkil mia't ma'u pa hota Auwali pia Amua teman ti makdena Lgona miy die, hota A'g emolmolla makwuri-makgalla la mela plinniohora!
source_text: The one who is all powerful/kings (lit. holds the octopus head and the flags top) also, they have not yet seen me so later I will return and come to meet you Luang people, I will be like a thief at night which you do not know about!

target_text: Lgon twahniorta!
source_text: Luang people pay attention!

target_text: Plola/Amin Itkalwiedni.
source_text: True Peace to you.
